record.title: Sarakhs Iran–Turkmenistan rail-freight COVID suspension
record.movement: Rail freight, including export and transit wagons
record.exceptions: No rail exception identified in reviewed accounts; no assertion about air or other routes.
record.imposing_authority: Government of Turkmenistan, according to Iranian officials
record.enforcement: Governor reports actual wagon movements; later customs statement corroborates resumption week.
record.relationship: Additional rail mode distinct from CC014 foreign-road-truck/driver restrictions; grouped within Turkmen pandemic frontier regime.
record.status_observation: Rail wagons reported crossing both directions June 18, 2020.
record.official_rationale: Turkmen government sought to prevent coronavirus spread, according to its notification reported by Iranian officials.
record.context: Iran–Turkmen road restrictions followed a different timetable; May rail readiness and June road-bridge inauguration are not endpoints.
record.uncertainty: Exact onset unresolved within April 1–2: Iran Press governor accounts give April 2, whereas a contemporary IRICA table gives April 1 for goods transport at the frontier and a later nCa/IRICA republication also gives April 1 but mixes wagon/truck vocabulary. Direct Iran Press retrieval returned 502; substantive indexed articles were reviewed. June 18 wagon movements are corroborated by full-text Tehran Times/IRICA. Original Turkmen closure order not retrieved.

historical.duration_note: No supported continuous operational interval for the stated scope. Do not compute a single-day duration until the April 1/April 2 onset discrepancy is reconciled. Closure is dated to April at present; competing days are retained in uncertainty. June 18 marks actual rail movement, not restoration of all road or passenger traffic.
